entries.title: Visa services paused at this embassy
entries.body: Since May 18, 2026, the U.S. Embassies in Juba, Kinshasa and Kampala have paused all visa services, including immigrant visas, because of the Ebola outbreak. No appointments can be scheduled. The State Department says it will update its website when scheduling resumes.

sources.label: State Department: Temporary Pause of Visa Operations

entries.title: Routine visa processing not available
entries.body: The State Department's notice of February 25, 2026, which is still posted, says that routine visa processing is not currently available at the U.S. Embassy in Beirut, which is prioritizing emergency services for U.S. citizens after the State Department ordered its non-emergency staff to leave on February 23. Applicants who had an interview scheduled in Beirut are to be emailed a new, later date. The State Department's scheduling tool has given Beirut the same month for spouses, children and parents of U.S. citizens, February 2026, since its April 2 update. Check lb.usembassy.gov/visas for updates.

sources.label: State Department: Limited Services Available at the U.S. Embassy in Lebanon

entries.title: No consular operations at this embassy
entries.body: The State Department says there are no consular operations in Khartoum. Its list of the embassies and consulates that process immigrant visas sends applicants from Sudan to the U.S. Embassy in Cairo.

entries.title: February notice of limited visa services is still posted
entries.body: On February 27, 2026, after authorizing the departure of non-emergency staff from Israel, the State Department said that routine visa processing was not currently available at the U.S. Embassy in Jerusalem and its Branch Office in Tel Aviv, and that applicants with interviews from March 2 to 6 would be emailed about rescheduling when services resumed. The notice is still posted, unchanged, and does not say whether services have resumed. The State Department's scheduling tool has since moved the month it gives Jerusalem for spouses, children and parents of U.S. citizens from February 2026, in its April 2 update, to August 2026, in its September 23 update. Check il.usembassy.gov/visas for the embassy's current status.

entries.title: Visa services moved to a regional hub
entries.body: Since August 1, 2026, routine visa services at this post, including immigrant visas, have moved to a regional hub. Citizens and residents of this country apply at the immigrant visa post the State Department designates for it instead.

sources.label: State Department: Realignment of U.S. Visa Services in Africa to Regional Hubs

entries.title: Immigrant visa interviews reportedly postponed for public charge training
entries.body: U.S. embassies and consulates have reportedly postponed immigrant visa interviews while their consular officers are trained on new public charge guidance, emailing applicants with interviews booked that they will be rescheduled. Reports differ on when this started. On August 27, the Associated Press quoted a State Department official saying the pause began in early August and was not expected to last beyond early to mid-September; a State Department statement quoted by Fox News on August 26 said its training initiative launched in early August. On September 8, Reuters reported that the pause came after the August 21 court ruling against the 75-country pause, that the government told a court interviews were rescheduled through August 31, that processing had resumed for Hungary and Poland while the pause continued elsewhere, and that it could last months, according to a person familiar with the matter. No report we have found says whether it is still in place at other posts. The State Department acknowledged the pause in a statement on August 25 but has posted no notice about it on its website. NVC and consulates may reschedule interviews, including ones already booked, while it lasts.

entries.title: Visa suspensions for 39 nationalities and Palestinian Authority travel documents
entries.body: Since January 1, 2026, Presidential Proclamation 10998 has suspended visas, with narrow exceptions: all visas for nationals of Afghanistan, Burma, Burkina Faso, Chad, the Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Eritrea, Haiti, Iran, Laos, Libya, Mali, Niger, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria and Yemen, and for anyone traveling on travel documents issued or endorsed by the Palestinian Authority; all immigrant visas, and B-1/B-2, F, M and J visas, for nationals of Angola, Antigua and Barbuda, Benin, Burundi, Cote d'Ivoire, Cuba, Dominica, Gabon, The Gambia, Malawi, Mauritania, Nigeria, Senegal, Tanzania, Togo, Tonga, Venezuela, Zambia and Zimbabwe; and all immigrant visas for nationals of Turkmenistan. Spouses, children and parents of U.S. citizens, and Afghan special immigrants, are no longer exempt. You can still apply and be scheduled for an interview, but the State Department says you may be ineligible for a visa. It depends on your nationality, not on the embassy: dual nationals applying with a passport of a nationality not subject to a suspension are exempt.

entries.title: 75-country immigrant visa pause has ended
entries.body: From January 21 to August 21, 2026, the State Department paused immigrant visa issuance to nationals of 75 countries. A court order in CLINIC v. Rubio ended the pause on August 21, 2026.

sources.label: State Department: Immigrant Visa Processing Updates for Nationalities at High Risk of Public Benefits Reliance

entries.title: Diversity visa issuance pause has ended
entries.body: In December 2025 the State Department paused diversity visa issuance: applicants could still apply and be interviewed, but no diversity visas were issued. As of August 28, 2026, under a court order in Medani v. Trump, the State Department says the pause is no longer in effect. Its notice, updated August 31, 2026, still carries the December announcement of the pause below that statement. Eligibility for a DV-2026 visa ends on September 30, 2026, the end of the fiscal year, and visas may run out before then.

entries.title: EB-2 visas for India used up until October 1
entries.body: The State Department has issued all the EB-2 immigrant visas available in fiscal year 2026 to applicants chargeable to India, so embassies and consulates may not issue these visas for the rest of the fiscal year. The annual limits reset on October 1, 2026, when they may resume issuing them to qualified applicants.

sources.label: State Department: India Per-Country Limit Reached in the EB-2 Category

entries.title: Unreserved EB-5 visas for India used up until October 1
entries.body: As of June 5, 2026, the State Department has issued all the unreserved EB-5 immigrant visas available in fiscal year 2026 to applicants chargeable to India: the C5, T5, I5, R5, RU and NU categories, not the rural, high-unemployment and infrastructure set-asides that this page also counts. Embassies and consulates may not issue visas in these categories for the rest of the fiscal year. The annual limits reset on October 1, 2026, when they may resume issuing them to qualified applicants.
